arxiv-2205-01481.title: Remote distribution of non-classical correlations over 1250 modes between a telecom photon and a 171 Yb 3+ :Y 2 SiO 5 crystal
arxiv-2205-01481.creator: M. Businger, L. Nicolas, T. Sanchez Mejia, A. Ferrier, P. Goldner, Mikael Afzelius
arxiv-2205-01481.description: Abstract Quantum repeaters based on heralded entanglement require quantum nodes that are able to generate multimode quantum correlations between memories and telecommunication photons. The communication rate scales linearly with the number of modes, yet highly multimode quantum storage remains challenging.

arxiv-2408-00100.creator: Roberto Vila, Helton Saulo, Felipe Quintino, Peter Zörnig

arxiv-2408-12688.title: Shadowing in the hyperspace of continua Thanks: 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification : Primary 37D10, 37B40, 37B45, Secondary 37B99.
arxiv-2408-12688.creator: Bernardo Carvalho and Udayan Darji
arxiv-2408-12688.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Bernardo Carvalho and Udayan Darji. We discuss whether classical examples of dynamical systems satisfying the shadowing property also satisfy the shadowing property for the induced map on the hyperspace of continua, obtaining both positive and negative results. We prove that transitive Anosov diffeomorphisms, or more generally continuum-wise hyperbolic homeomorphisms, do not satisfy the shadowing property for the induced map on the hyperspace of continua.

arxiv-2408-17135.title: TIMotion: Temporal and Interactive Framework for Efficient Human-Human Motion Generation
arxiv-2408-17135.creator: Yabiao Wang, Shuo Wang, Jiangning Zhang, Ke Fan, Jiafu Wu, Zhucun Xue, Yong Liu
arxiv-2408-17135.description: Abstract Human-human motion generation is essential for understanding humans as social beings. Current methods fall into two main categories: single-person-based methods and separate modeling-based methods. To delve into this field, we abstract the overall generation process into a general framework MetaMotion, which consists of two phases: temporal modeling and interaction mixing.

arxiv-2409-06020.title: Peephole Optimization for Quantum Approximate Synthesis
arxiv-2409-06020.creator: Joseph Clark, Himanshu Thapliyal
arxiv-2409-06020.description: Abstract Peephole optimization of quantum circuits provides a method of leveraging standard circuit synthesis approaches into scalable quantum circuit optimization. One application of this technique partitions an entire circuit into a series of peepholes and produces multiple approximations of each partitioned subcircuit. A single approximation of each subcircuit is then selected to form optimized result circuits.

arxiv-2506-06866.title: Safe : Finding Sparse and Flat Minima to Improve Pruning
arxiv-2506-06866.creator: Dongyeop Lee, Kwanhee Lee, Jinseok Chung, Namhoon Lee
arxiv-2506-06866.description: Abstract Sparsifying neural networks often suffers from seemingly inevitable performance degradation, and it remains challenging to restore the original performance despite much recent progress. Motivated by recent studies in robust optimization, we aim to tackle this problem by finding subnetworks that are both sparse and flat at the same time.

pmc-10944877.creator: Cassandra Falckenhayn, Agata Bienkowska, Jörn Söhle, Katrin Wegner, Guenter Raddatz, Boris Kristof, Dirk Kuck, Ralf Siegner, Ronny Kaufmann, Julia Korn, Sascha Baumann, Daniela Lange, Andreas Schepky, Henry Völzke, Lars Kaderali, Marc Winnefeld, Frank Lyko, Elke Grönniger
pmc-10944877.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Changes in DNA methylation patterning have been reported to be a key hallmark of aged human skin. The altered DNA methylation patterns are correlated with deregulated gene expression and impaired tissue functionality, leading to the well-known skin aging phenotype. Searching for small molecules, which correct the aged methylation pattern therefore represents a novel and attractive strategy for the identification of anti-aging compounds.

pmc-12508343.title: Bibliometric analysis of global research trends in delivery systems for breast cancer immunotherapy
pmc-12508343.creator: Jun-Yi Yang, Xin-Yu Li, Si-Lu Xiang, Xiao-Yi Wang
pmc-12508343.description: BackgroundBreast cancer (BC) immunotherapy exhibits disappointingly low response rates and faces significant challenges including systemic toxicity and poor tumor penetration, while delivery systems (DSs) offer revolutionary capacity to enhance efficacy and minimize adverse effects. Despite exponential growth in DSs research for BC immunotherapy, comprehensive bibliometric analyses examining the global research landscape and strategic development directions remain absent.
